body: @mdjermanovic But at least I think it should be disclosed in documents. And if I make a PR about this, will it be able to be accepted?

> @mdjermanovic But at least I think it should be disclosed in documents. And if I make a PR about this, will it be able to be accepted?

Yes, we can accept documentation updates for this rule. PR is welcome!

@mdjermanovic Can I directly remove the codes about `getOwnPropertyNames` in the rule file? So the rule **will work fine and won't break peoples' work anymore**. Even further, I worte [a plugin](https://github.com/AnnAngela/eslint-plugin/blob/master/lib/rules/prefer-reflect.js) to improve the rule, if you don't mind, I can merge that (of course I will keep the original options schema).

If the anwser is "no", I will make a PR to change the document only instead.
The appropriate Reflect method you should be using here is called `Reflect.ownKeys`.

@AnnAngela per our [rule deprecation policy](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/user-guide/rule-deprecation), we're not making any changes to deprecated rules. In this case, we can make an exception to describe a workaround in the docs, but we're definitely not making any changes in the code.

@ljharb `Reflect.ownKeys` includes symbols, so it's not the same as `Object.getOwnPropertyNames `?
@mdjermanovic that's a fair point, but it's just `Reflect.ownKeys(x).filter(x => typeof x === 'string')` ¯\\\_(ツ)_/¯

> that's a fair point, but it's just `Reflect.ownKeys(x).filter(x => typeof x === 'string')` ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

That would work, but this rule wasn't intended to suggest replacements of such complexity, so I think it's fine to add a note in the docs that `Object.getOwnPropertyNames` was added by mistake.
@mdjermanovic OK, I will make a PR to change the documents only.
